# entrepot_waiver (Resource)

A vulnerability waiver: findings matching it are ignored when deciding whether to quarantine a component. Repositories and components are matched with globs. Expired waivers stay defined (and in state) but no longer apply.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Accept one vulnerability in one component until the upgrade lands.
resource "entrepot_waiver" "xz" {
  vuln_id           = "CVE-2024-3094"
  component_pattern = "xz-utils@5.6.*"
  reason            = "Not shipped in production images; tracked in SEC-123"
  expires_at        = "2026-12-31T23:59:59Z"
}

# Ignore every finding in sandbox repositories.
resource "entrepot_waiver" "sandbox" {
  vuln_id            = "*"
  repository_pattern = "sandbox-*"
  reason             = "Experimental repositories are not scanned for policy"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `vuln_id` (String) Vulnerability ID, e.g. `CVE-2024-3094` or `GHSA-…`, or `*` for any vulnerability (then a repository or component pattern is required).

### Optional

- `component_pattern` (String) Glob over `name` or `name@version` of components, e.g. `lodash@4.17.*`. Default `*`.
- `expires_at` (String) When the waiver stops applying, as an RFC 3339 timestamp (e.g. `2026-12-31T23:59:59Z`). Unset: never expires.
- `reason` (String) Why the finding is accepted (shown in the UI and audit log).
- `repository_pattern` (String) Glob over repository names. Default `*`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `created_by` (String) Principal that created the waiver.
- `id` (String) Server-assigned waiver ID (used for import).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Waivers are imported by their server-assigned ID.
terraform import entrepot_waiver.xz 3f0c2a8e-6b1d-4f7a-9c55-2d8e1b7a4c90
```
